name: Content Cloud
dek: One workspace for planning, publishing, and tracking content.

at_a_glance.role: Sole UX/UI designer, end to end
at_a_glance.scope: Research, competitor analysis, user journeys, design system, hi-fi UI, usability testing
at_a_glance.hard_part: Marketing an analytics product to creators who distrust dashboards, without hiding the data behind hype.
at_a_glance.look_for: How each landing section pairs a creator pain point with the exact tool that answers it, ending in one clear action.

problem.claim_h2: Creators post constantly and still fly blind
problem.thesis: Scheduling tools tell creators when they posted, not whether any of it worked or what to make next.
problem.body: Competitor platforms each solve one slice: scheduling, calendars, or reporting. Creators end up stitching tools together and still guessing at what to post, when to post it, and why growth stalls.
bullets: No clear signal on which content types actually move an audience.
Shallow analytics that describe the past instead of guiding the next post.
Planning, insights, and collaboration split across separate, costly tools.
problem.research_note: Desk research covered six competitors including Later, Hootsuite, Buffer, CoSchedule, Sprout Social, and ContentStudio, mapped by features, strengths, and gaps.

design.claim_h2: Every section earns the next scroll
design.intro: The site walks a skeptical creator from identity to proof to community, and each section closes with a single unmistakable action.

figures.caption: A glitch-treated wordmark opens the site, claiming a creator-native identity before any feature talk begins.
figures.alt: Hero screen with a navy navigation bar and a glitching chromatic Futuri Content Cloud logo over a deep blue background.

figures.caption: The Tools page leads with the real analytics dashboard, so the product proof is the marketing, not a stock illustration.
figures.alt: Tools page showing a dashboard mockup with a donut chart of total audience by channel and a stacked growth graph, followed by a trending content module.

figures.caption: The audience section names the fear of posting into the void, then answers it with a free dashboard as the low-risk first step.
figures.alt: Landing section with lime headline reading you gotta know your audience to grow your audience, portrait photos in circles, and a free dashboard button.

figures.caption: Community gets its own section with Discord front and center, positioning support as a feature rather than a footer link.
figures.alt: Purple section with a Discord icon, headline you don't have to do it alone, and a yellow start-for-free button over a wave pattern.

figures.caption: Six numbered pillars beside the live dashboard compress the whole pitch into one closing summary before the final call to action.
figures.alt: Section titled what is Futuri Content Cloud listing six numbered benefits next to an analytics dashboard screenshot with a glowing button below.

validation.honest_line: Moderated sessions confirmed people could navigate the site and find each answer, but only a live product could show whether the insights change what creators actually post.

appendix.framing: The system underneath the marketing surface: a componentized navigation, card, and dropdown library on a 12-column grid, and tonal ramps for every brand color.

figures.caption: Nav states, cards, and dropdowns are specced as components on a documented 1440px grid, keeping four pages visually consistent.
figures.alt: Component sheet showing four navigation bar hover states, three photo cards, collapsed and expanded dropdowns, and a 12-column desktop grid diagram.

figures.caption: Each brand hue ships as an eight-step ramp with hex values, so contrast choices on dark surfaces are picks, not guesses.
figures.alt: Vivid Cerulean color ramp from a saturated 700 step to near white, each swatch labeled with its name and hex code.
